about: The closed list of physics material ids (AST-05, setup-asset-pipeline design decision 6, physics review R3). Every collision shape's 'material' and every material slot's 'physics' must be an id of 'materials', or 'surface:<id>' naming one of the thirteen ground surfaces (S01-S13, knowledge §7.2) for a shape that stands in for ground; lib/meta.validate refuses anything else. New ids are added here with physics sign-off, never in a generator: the phase-1 sign-off is openspec/changes/p1-pipeline-hardening/review-materials.md. A plain id never shares a surface's name. The values are the physics engineer's to tune in phases 3 and 6.

fields.friction_static: mu_s of the drone's polymer parts on the dry material
fields.stiffness_n_per_m: contact compliance of the surface; absent means rigid
fields.damping_ratio: zeta of that compliance; present with stiffness_n_per_m
fields.edge_radius_m: the radius the fiber bends over at a box's arris; a capsule, cylinder or sphere always uses its own radius, and a snag's radius_m overrides both; null means the material never carries an arris (it is only used on round shapes)
fields.break_stress_pa: optional: the bending rupture stress of a member on a capsule or cylinder; the contact law derives the break moment from the shape's own radius, M_b = break_stress_pa * pi * r^3 / 4, past which the shape stops resisting for the rest of the flight and a 'break' event is logged, and a hook snag of the material lets go at the same moment; absent means the member never breaks
fields.label: where the numbers stand: pilot, measured, published, derived or assumed
fields.rationale: the source or the calculation, as recorded in the physics review

steel.label: assumed
steel.rationale: carried from surfaces-review §5 (polymer on dry mild steel, rolled or sawn edge)

sheet_metal.label: assumed
sheet_metal.rationale: carried: 0.5 mm corrugated sheet over a 1 m purlin span; its half-thickness edge cuts the fiber

timber.label: assumed
timber.rationale: carried; a batten asset may override with ≈ 1e5 N/m

masonry.label: assumed
masonry.rationale: carried: brick, block, render; a worn arris

concrete.label: assumed
concrete.rationale: plastic feet on cast concrete sit in the published 0.5–0.7 band; a cast arris. Broken edges and rebar are 'edge' snags with their own radius. Also lifted asphalt slabs and kerbs (review-materials.md: 'asphalt' is a surface id only)

glass.label: assumed
glass.rationale: plastic on glass; a broken pane edge is a blade. Also glazed porcelain (insulators: cylinders, so the edge is their own radius). Breakability of a pane is a later plate model (review P3-6)

cable.label: assumed
cable.rationale: carried; rigid locally, the span compliance T = w·L²/(8·sag) comes from the wire geometry; the edge radius is the wire's own

foliage.label: derived
foliage.rationale: a 20 mm green branch at 1 m, E ≈ 10 GPa (published 8–12 GPa for green wood), I = πd⁴/64 = 7.85e-9 m⁴, k = 3EI/L³ ≈ 236 N/m; ζ assumed for a leafy branch; the edge radius is the branch's own

bark.label: assumed
bark.rationale: live trunks and limbs: furrowed or plated bark interlocks with a printed foot's layer ridges, so above sawn timber (0.45/0.35); the published 0.2–0.5 of polymers on wood is for planed faces, and bark is not planed; rigid; trunks and limbs are capsules, so the fiber bends over the member's own radius, never an arris

twig.label: derived
twig.rationale: the crown contact shell over the 5–10 mm twig cards (no capsules): one 10 mm green twig 0.8 m long, E ≈ 10 GPa, I = πd⁴/64 = 4.91e-10 m⁴, k = 3EI/L³ ≈ 29 N/m, so a 20 N push goes through the shell to the branch capsules, which is the point; μ as foliage, ζ assumed lower for bare twigs; the fiber bends over the thinnest twig the shell stands for, radius 2.5 mm

deadwood.label: assumed
deadwood.rationale: dead trees, broken tops, fallen branches, brush, logs, wattle rods: friction as weathered timber; rigid until it snaps at M_b = σ_b·π·r³/4 from the member's own radius (a 10 mm dead twig: 3.9 N·m, 8 N at a 0.5 m tip), σ_b 40 MPa assumed under the published 60–110 MPa rupture of dry hardwood for checking and decay; members are capsules, so the fiber bends over their own radius

asbestos_cement.label: assumed
asbestos_cement.rationale: slate sheets and fragments: a cement-bound surface under a polymer foot, as concrete; a 5.8 mm 8-wave sheet (published) with E ≈ 15 GPa and I ≈ t·a²/2 per metre of 40 mm waves answers a foot over a 0.6 m batten span at ≈ 1e6 N/m, so it is rigid and the leg sets the bounce; the edge is the sheet's half thickness; a landing loads a sound sheet to ≈ 0.4 MPa against a published rupture ≥ 16 MPa, so plate breakage is a crash case for a later plate model (review P3-6)

straw.label: derived
straw.rationale: thatch, hay, a stack, straw carried by a mesh or a roof: the belt_straw mat (modulus 4 kPa, surfaces.json) 0.125 m deep under the 15 mm reference foot, km = modulus·π(b/2 + D/2)²/D ≈ 490 N/m; μ and ζ carried from that mat; the fiber sinks into a straw edge, so the bend radius is the soil-lip figure 0.02 m (assumed); bundle ends are hook snags the generator writes. Straw over ground is surface:belt_straw, not this id

fabric.label: assumed
fabric.rationale: tarps, curtains, mattresses, sofas, seats, a canvas tilt, greenhouse film: a polymer foot on woven PE or canvas, above the published 0.2–0.4 of plastic on plastic for the weave; stiffness from the sheets' 50–100 mm sink of a mattress or seat under the drone's 49 N (490–980 N/m); ζ for a damped cushion that does not bounce; the edge is a hem or a fold

rubber.label: assumed
rubber.rationale: tyres: a polymer foot on tread rubber sits in the published 0.6–0.9 band; tread rubber (E ≈ 5 MPa, 10 mm) under the 15 mm foot compresses at EA/t ≈ 9e4 N/m and the carcass flexes under it, 5e4 N/m together; ζ for rubber hysteresis; a tyre is a cylinder, so the fiber bends over its own radius, and 10 mm stands for a rubber box's rounded shoulder

plastic.label: assumed
plastic.rationale: PVC frames, crates, housings, trim, bumper covers, packaging, EPS remnants: polymer on polymer in the published 0.2–0.4 band; profiles and crates are rigid under a foot, and a 3 mm bumper cover that flexes (≈ 1e2 N/m over 0.5 m) has the steel beam behind it; a moulded edge 1–2 mm; EPS yields at 70–100 kPa (published grades), under the 141 kPa of the 25 N reference foot, a deviation accepted for remnants (review-materials.md)

mesh.label: derived
mesh.rationale: chain-link bays as thin boxes: a 2 mm galvanised mesh strung at ≈ 200 N/m (assumed) over a 3 m bay answers a drone-sized point load as a membrane, k ≈ 2πT/ln(a/r) ≈ 800 N/m, so the drone is caught, not bounced; ζ assumed for link friction; μ as steel; the fiber bends over a 1 mm wire, a cut risk
